overallNotes: This source is a single defined term ("Consolidated Net Income") in the Section 1.01 Definitions article, not an operative permission/restriction rule, so no WireRule or WireSharedCapacity outputs apply; only one WireDefinition is emitted.

All 47 frozen-inventory items were consumed on the specific expression node carrying their value/meaning within the calculationExpression tree; four items with real drafting ambiguity or an unresolved dependent term were additionally cross-noted in inventoryDispositions for reviewer visibility even though also consumed in the tree.

'Net Income' and 'Transactions' were resolved via getDefinition and used as-is; 'Guarantor'/'Guarantors' was attempted via getDefinition and getDefinitionDependencies but is not declared anywhere in this instrument, so the Guarantor carve-out in exclusion (6) is preserved structurally but its membership is unresolved.

The $5,000,000 cap on unsuccessful/non-consummated transaction costs in exclusion (11) is a self-contained cap within this single definition's own formula (not shared across independent baskets), so it is modeled with a MIN node rather than a WireSharedCapacity.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: "calculationExpression": { "kind": "UNSUPPORTED", ... "reason": "SUBTRACT operands do not type-check together" ... }, and top-level "sufficiency": "PARTIAL"
findings.verifierReasoning: The proposed IR's root-level calculationExpression.kind is literally "UNSUPPORTED" — the entire top-level SUBTRACT (Net Income plus inclusions, minus the sum of exclusions) is flagged as failing to type-check, and that failure cascades from a chain of nested UNSUPPORTED nodes (the exclusions SUM itself, the clause-6 boolean-restriction logic, etc.). In other words, as compiled, no numeric value for Consolidated Net Income can actually be computed from this expression tree at all — it is not merely missing a few line items, it is entirely non-evaluable at the root. Despite this, the definition's own "sufficiency" field is set to "PARTIAL" rather than something signaling total non-computability (e.g. UNSUPPORTED/MISSING_CONTEXT at the top level). "PARTIAL" naturally reads as "mostly usable, some gaps," which could lead a downstream consumer (e.g., a Restricted Payments, Excess Cash Flow, or Available Amount calculation that references Consolidated Net Income) to treat this definition as largely reliable and either silently receive an error, a null, or a wrong default value, rather than recognizing that the compiled representation currently provides no usable formula whatsoever for this heavily-used defined term. This is a disclosure-accuracy problem independent of whether the individual line items were correctly identified (which, on inspection, they largely were) — the aggregate computability status is materially overstated by the chosen sufficiency label.','}

findings.verifierReasoning: The deterministic pass flagged that the $5,000,000 amount does not appear anywhere in the compiled IR. On manual inspection, the value is in fact present, correctly scoped as a MIN-cap applied only to charges/nonrecurring merger costs from unsuccessful or non-consummated transactions (matching the source proviso), and not applied to the general (successful-transaction) fee addback in the same clause. This appears to be a false positive from the deterministic scanner, likely because the value is nested several levels deep inside a subtree whose parent node is marked UNSUPPORTED due to unrelated type-checking failures elsewhere in the tree, and the scanner may not have traversed into 'attemptedStructure' branches of UNSUPPORTED nodes. I am not treating this as a standalone material finding because the substantive representation of the $5,000,000 cap is correct; however, because the enclosing expression graph is non-evaluable (see the sufficiency-mismatch finding above), this correctly-modeled figure is not currently actionable in practice either.
